narration: Say five smart people meet,
to decide one plan.
Each one doubts it.
Nobody says so.
beats.visual_intent: a small meeting room seen like a stage set: five outlined people round one table, a single plan sheet in the middle; above each head a small thought bubble, folded shut, that only the viewer notices

grounding.claim: the five people, the meeting and the plan are an invented illustration

narration: Agreed. The plan passes.
Every hand goes up.
How do smart people do that?
And what stops it?
beats.visual_intent: hands rise one at a time in stepped, drawn-frame timing; on the last hand a hand-lettered stamp, Agreed, lands on the plan sheet while the five folded bubbles stay shut

grounding.claim: the vote is part of the invented illustration

narration: Meet Dana. She runs the team.
She opens with what she wants,
launch by the end of the quarter.
beats.visual_intent: the stamp peels back off the sheet as time steps backwards; Dana stands at the head of the table and writes the goal on a board behind her, Launch: end of quarter; the other four turn towards it

grounding.claim: Dana, her team and the launch goal are invented

narration: One colleague agrees, fast.
Great, let's do it.
The room now has a direction.
beats.visual_intent: a speech bubble from the colleague beside Dana; the plan sheet on the table slides a little towards the board, as if the whole table has tilted towards yes

grounding.claim: a leader stating a preferred option early tends to narrow what the group discusses
the colleague and the line are invented

narration: Inside each head, a doubt.
Testing isn't done.
Support isn't trained.
The client hasn't seen it.
Even the fast yes doubts the date.
beats.visual_intent: the four folded bubbles open one at a time on their words, each holding one drawn object with its one-word label: a half-ticked checklist, a headset, a sealed envelope, a calendar page with a question mark; the characters cannot see each other's bubbles

grounding.claim: the four doubts are invented for the illustration

narration: Each one looks around.
Calm faces.
And decides, I must be the only one.
beats.visual_intent: slow down here: the camera passes from face to face; each person sees only calm faces and closed bubbles, and on the word only their own bubble shrinks and folds shut

grounding.claim: people who privately doubt something can assume everyone else accepts it
people often stay quiet expecting that raising a concern is pointless or costly

narration: So nobody says it.
Silence starts to look like yes.
Hands go up.
beats.visual_intent: the same hands rise again in stepped timing, now seen from the doubters' side; as each hand goes up, its bubble flattens into a closed lid; Agreed lands on the sheet a second time

grounding.claim: members keep doubts to themselves, and silence is taken as agreement

narration: Weeks later, the launch slips.
Every one of those doubts comes true.
beats.visual_intent: a torn-paper jump forward in time, calendar pages tearing off in steps; each private doubt from the opening comes back as the real problem on the same object, one after another: the checklist covered in red marks, the headset ringing, the envelope returned, the calendar date crossed out

grounding.claim: the failed launch is part of the invented illustration

narration: Nobody in that room was foolish.
Every doubt was right.
None of them reached the table.
beats.visual_intent: back in the room after the failure: the five people sit in the same places, and the four doubt objects hang above them in a quiet row, none of them touching the table

grounding.claim: the cause is the drive to keep agreement, not a lack of intelligence

beats.misconception: groupthink happens to weaker teams; a smart team would catch it

narration: The psychologist Irving Janis studied this.
He developed the idea of groupthink.
The drive to agree,
beating a hard look at the plan.
beats.visual_intent: a black turn card, then the word Groupthink hand-lettered large on a sign that hangs over the meeting room door; under it, a small balance where drive to agree outweighs a hard look on the narrated words

grounding.claim: Irving Janis developed groupthink into a theory, studying capable decision makers
groupthink is a close-knit group's drive for agreement overriding a realistic look at alternatives
his cases involved experienced, capable decision makers

narration: The evidence for it is mixed.
Call it a pattern, not a law.
Leader first. Doubts private. Silence as yes.
beats.visual_intent: the room again, held in one layout; the three parts light up in turn on their words: the board with Dana's goal, the four folded bubbles, the raised hands; each calms as the next lights

grounding.claim: the evidence for Janis's full model is mixed; it is a useful description rather than a proven law
a leader making their preference known early is a condition linked to groupthink
self-censorship and the illusion of unanimity

narration: Keep those four doubts in mind.
Now, rewind.
beats.visual_intent: the whole meeting runs backwards in steps, like flipped pages: the stamp lifts, hands come down, the goal on the board erases itself, until the table is clear and the four folded bubbles wait above the same heads

grounding.claim: the replay is part of the invented illustration

recall.prompt: keep the four private doubts from the first meeting in mind: testing, support, the client, the date

narration: Same people. First, Dana speaks last.
With nothing to follow,
the fast yes asks about the date.
beats.visual_intent: same room, same five people, rewound: the board behind Dana stays blank and she sits back; with nothing to follow, the colleague beside her opens his own bubble and the calendar page with its question mark comes down onto the table as a written note, the first of four

grounding.claim: a leader staying impartial at the start, holding back their preference, lets others raise alternatives

narration: Second, everyone writes a view first.
Before anyone talks.
Out comes, testing isn't done.
beats.visual_intent: five cards slide out and are written on at the same moment, heads down; turned over together, one card shows the half-ticked checklist; it joins the first note on the table

grounding.claim: writing views down before discussion keeps judgements independent and reduces the pull of whoever speaks first

narration: Third, one person is named the critic.
Objecting is a job, not a risk.
Out comes the support worry.
beats.visual_intent: a small hand-lettered tent card, Critic, is set in front of one person; the headset comes out of the support person's bubble and down onto the table as the third note

grounding.claim: giving one member the job of critical evaluator makes objections expected rather than risky

narration: Fourth, a premortem.
Imagine it has already failed.
Why?
Out comes the client nobody asked.
beats.visual_intent: the board shows an imagined future page, the plan stamped failed, framed as pretend with a dotted border; the team writes reasons under it, and the sealed envelope comes down as the fourth note

grounding.claim: a premortem asks the team to imagine the plan has failed and write down why, before deciding

narration: Nobody got braver.
The meeting made doubt the expected thing.
And the plan gets fixed, before it ships.
beats.visual_intent: the same five people, the same nervous postures as before; the four notes sit on the table where the empty Agreed stamp was; the plan sheet morphs into an amended plan with the date moved and lines added

grounding.claim: the habits make raising doubts the expected move rather than relying on individual courage
people stay quiet when they expect speaking up to cost them
the fixed plan is part of the invented illustration, not a guaranteed result

beats.misconception: the fix is braver people who just speak up

narration: Your turn.
Next meeting, Dana says what she wants first.
Then, any objections? Silence.
Speak last, write first, a critic, or a premortem?
Pause, and pick.
beats.visual_intent: a new meeting in the same room, frozen at the quiet after any objections; the four habits sit beside it as four small objects (a blank board, a card, the Critic tent card, the failed page) for the viewer to choose from; a real silent pause

grounding.claim: the next meeting is part of the invented illustration

recall.prompt: Dana has already said what she wants, asked for objections, and got silence. Which habit do you reach for now?
recall.answer: have everyone write down, on their own, one reason the plan could fail, then read them out: writing first, aimed like a premortem
recall.tempting_wrong: take the quiet as a yes, or ask for objections again: silence is not agreement, and asking out loud asks each doubter to be the first and only one to object

narration: Speaking last is gone. She spoke.
Asking again asks someone to go first.
Instead, everyone writes why it could fail.
Then they read them out.
beats.visual_intent: the blank board greys out on its words; cards slide out round the table and are written at once, then turned over together, so the doubts appear at the same moment and no single person goes first

grounding.claim: writing views first keeps judgements independent of whoever speaks first
imagining the plan failed and writing why makes raising doubts part of the task
silence is not agreement; doubters assume they are alone
people expect speaking up alone to cost them

narration: One said doubt can make the next easier.
So pick one decision this week.
Choose a habit before it starts.
If you run it, speak last.
beats.visual_intent: the view widens from Dana's table to a wall calendar of the viewer's week; one meeting slot gets a small hand-lettered tag for a chosen habit

grounding.claim: in conformity studies, one other person disagreeing made it much easier for others to disagree
a leader holding back their view lets others raise alternatives

narration: Back at Dana's table,
the same four doubts are there.
This time, on the table.
The silence was never agreement.
beats.visual_intent: callback to the opening frame, same angle and same five people: where the folded bubbles were, the four notes now sit on the table in front of them, and the Agreed stamp is replaced by the amended plan; the frame rests

grounding.claim: silence is taken as agreement under groupthink, though members privately doubt
the closing scene is part of the invented illustration

recall.prompt: the first meeting: every doubt was there all along; it just had nowhere to go
